title: UnitedHealth/Optum Impact Pro population-health algorithm racial bias
system_purpose: Score patients by predicted future cost and utilization to flag who should be enrolled in extra care-management programs
decision_impact: The risk score determined who was offered additional case-management support, i.e. access to extra clinical attention
affected_groups: Black patients;chronically ill health plan members;care-management program applicants
verified_facts: Obermeyer et al. (Science, 2019-10-25) found that at equal algorithm risk scores, Black patients were significantly sicker than White patients because the algorithm used healthcare cost as a proxy for health need. New York's DFS and DOH sent a joint letter (2019-10-25) to UnitedHealth stating the tool 'significantly underestimates health needs for black patients.'
reported_harm: Reduced likelihood that equally-sick Black patients were flagged for extra care management; regulators called this a discriminatory outcome regardless of intent
quantitative_evidence: Correcting the bias would raise the share of Black patients flagged for extra help from 17.7% to 46.5% (Obermeyer et al. 2019); neither source discloses the total number of enrollees affected in practice
limitations: The study covers one large national algorithm used across many health systems, not this product; the NY DFS/DOH letter is a regulatory inquiry demanding investigation, not a completed enforcement finding, so the regulatory outcome is not fully resolved in the public record

title: Epic Sepsis Model external validation at Michigan Medicine
system_purpose: Predict onset of sepsis in hospitalized patients from EHR data to trigger a clinical alert
decision_impact: A positive alert was meant to prompt earlier clinician evaluation and treatment for sepsis
affected_groups: hospitalized patients;patients at risk of sepsis;treating clinicians
verified_facts: Wong et al. (JAMA Internal Medicine, 2021-06-21) externally validated the Epic Sepsis Model on 27,697 patients across 38,455 hospitalizations at Michigan Medicine and found an AUC of 0.63 and only 33% sensitivity at the recommended alert threshold, far below Epic's reported 0.76-0.83. A STAT News investigation (2021-07-26) reported clinicians describing frequent false alarms and missed cases in real-world use.
reported_harm: Missed early sepsis detection reduces the chance of timely treatment, and frequent false alarms can cause alert fatigue that makes clinicians less likely to act on any alert, including true ones
quantitative_evidence: AUC 0.63 (95% CI 0.62-0.64) and 33% sensitivity at a score threshold of 6 in the JAMA Internal Medicine external validation, versus Epic's reported 0.76-0.83 AUC in internal validation
limitations: Findings come from a single academic health system over an 11-month window and may not generalize to every hospital's implementation or threshold configuration; STAT News' specific false-alarm and missed-case figures are behind a paywall and not independently re-verified here

title: NEDA Tessa chatbot harmful eating-disorder advice
system_purpose: Provide automated, script-based support to people seeking help for eating disorders, intended to supplement and then replace a human-staffed helpline
decision_impact: The chatbot's responses were the direct advice a vulnerable user received in place of, or before reaching, a human counselor
affected_groups: people seeking eating-disorder support;helpline callers;NEDA staff and volunteers
verified_facts: NPR (2023-06-08) and NBC News reported NEDA disabled the Tessa chatbot on 2023-05-30, less than 24 hours after receiving screenshots showing it recommended losing '1 to 2 pounds per week,' staying under a set daily calorie count, and tracking a calorie deficit. NEDA's CEO confirmed this content was against NEDA policy and was pulled 'until further notice.'
reported_harm: Calorie-restriction and weight-loss advice given to people seeking eating-disorder support is widely regarded by clinicians as unsafe for that population and contrary to the service's own stated policy
quantitative_evidence: No public count of how many users received the harmful messages was disclosed; NBC News reported NEDA citing a 600% traffic surge and 'nefarious activity from bad actors' around the same period, with no independent verification of that claim
limitations: NEDA's own explanation raised the possibility that some harmful outputs were prompted by adversarial user behavior rather than a default script failure, so the exact cause is not fully confirmed in the public record; no full technical incident report was published
